finding: At the memory ceiling, Redis's default search-on-oom setting (return) answers a search with zero results and no error. A turn would read that as nothing found.
severity: medium: reachable only with the index at its memory ceiling; it would turn an outage of capacity into a false negative in the evidence a model is given
how_found: A K2 smoke through the real route, with memory held over the ceiling, found no records for a term it had just found; a direct probe on the pinned image then isolated the setting.

probe.writes_at_the_ceiling: refused with OOM under each setting

change: src/optimus/acp/local_infra.py _memory_server_args adds --search-on-oom IGNORE. Codex review 21 agreed with IGNORE over FAIL: writes are still refused and searches keep answering. It does not guarantee adequate RAM or latency at scale; Release B's K2 measures those.

proof_at_smoke_scale.source_clean_when_run: Yes. The only uncommitted file was retrieval.json, which another run was writing.
proof_at_smoke_scale.before: An earlier smoke, on the default setting, read readable_while_full false; it was not kept as a clean record, so the probe below is the evidence for the default's behaviour.
proof_at_smoke_scale.note: Smoke scale only: a few records. The real run is k2.json.

upgrade_consequence: A container created before this change has the old arguments and now fails the launch's configuration check with 'it runs Redis with other settings'; restarting it does not change them. It needs removing and recreating, which rebuilds nothing but its own data, since the index is rebuildable. The only such container was removed at CP3's end.
